english_text: Health education is a lifelong journey of learning and growth.
Using a condom correctly every time you have sex prevents HIV and STIs.
Condoms are available free of charge at all public health clinics.
Both male and female condoms are available at the clinic.
Use a new condom every time you have sexual intercourse.
Check the expiry date on the condom before using it.
Do not use oil-based lubricants with latex condoms.
Water-based lubricants are safe to use with condoms.
PrEP is a medication that prevents HIV in HIV-negative people.
Ask your clinic about PrEP if you are at high risk of HIV.
PEP is an emergency medication taken after possible HIV exposure.
PEP must be started within seventy-two hours of exposure.
PEP must be taken for twenty-eight days without missing doses.
Seek medical attention immediately after a possible HIV exposure.
Get tested for HIV and STIs regularly if you are sexually active.
Knowing your HIV status protects you and your partner.
Encourage your partner to get tested for HIV together.
Disclosure of your HIV status to your partner is important.
Support is available for people who need help with disclosure.
Sexually transmitted infections increase the risk of HIV transmission.
Treat all sexually transmitted infections promptly and completely.
Symptoms of STIs include discharge, sores, burning, and pain.
Some STIs have no symptoms and can only be detected by testing.
Regular STI testing is recommended for sexually active people.
Inform your sexual partner if you are diagnosed with an STI.
Both partners must be treated for an STI at the same time.
Avoid sexual contact until both partners have completed STI treatment.
Reducing the number of sexual partners reduces the risk of STIs.
Mutual faithfulness between tested partners reduces HIV risk.
Alcohol and drug use increase the risk of unsafe sexual behaviour.
Avoid making sexual decisions when under the influence of alcohol.
Sexual violence increases the risk of HIV and STI transmission.
Seek medical care immediately after sexual violence.
Post-exposure prophylaxis is available after sexual violence.
Report sexual violence to the police and seek legal support.
Support is available for survivors of sexual violence.
Cervical cancer is caused by the human papillomavirus.
The HPV vaccine protects against cervical cancer.
Girls should receive the HPV vaccine before becoming sexually active.
Regular cervical screening detects abnormal cells before they become cancer.
Women should have a cervical smear test every three years.
Hepatitis B is transmitted through sexual contact and blood.
Vaccination against hepatitis B protects your liver.
Herpes is a lifelong viral infection that can be managed with medication.
Gonorrhoea and chlamydia are bacterial infections that are treatable.
Syphilis is a serious STI that can be cured with antibiotics.
Untreated syphilis can cause serious damage to the heart and brain.
Trichomoniasis is a common STI that is easily treated.
All STIs are treatable and most are curable with the right medication.
Do not be ashamed to seek treatment for a sexually transmitted infection.
Healthcare workers treat all STI patients with confidentiality and respect.
Sexual health is an important part of your overall health and wellbeing.
Open communication with your partner about sexual health is important.
Healthy relationships are built on trust, respect, and communication.
Gender-based violence is a public health issue that requires urgent action.
Seek help if you are experiencing violence in your relationship.
Support services for gender-based violence are available at the clinic.
Every person deserves to be in a safe and healthy relationship.
Your sexual health decisions affect your long-term health and wellbeing.
Mental health is a state of wellbeing in which you can cope with daily life.
One in four people will experience a mental health problem in their lifetime.
Mental health problems are common and nothing to be ashamed of.
Depression is more than just feeling sad — it is a medical condition.
Symptoms of depression include persistent sadness, loss of interest, and fatigue.
Anxiety is a feeling of excessive worry and fear that affects daily life.
Symptoms of anxiety include restlessness, racing heart, and difficulty sleeping.
Post-traumatic stress disorder can develop after a traumatic event.
Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness that affects thinking and behaviour.
Bipolar disorder causes extreme mood swings between highs and lows.
Mental health conditions are caused by a combination of factors.
Stress, trauma, genetics, and substance abuse can affect mental health.
Mental health problems can affect anyone regardless of age or background.
Children and adolescents can also experience mental health problems.
Older adults are at increased risk of depression and cognitive decline.
People living with chronic illness are at higher risk of depression.
Substance abuse and mental health problems often occur together.
Seek help early if you notice changes in your mood or behaviour.
Talk to your doctor or nurse if you are struggling with your mental health.
Mental health treatment includes counselling, medication, and support groups.
Counselling helps you understand and manage your thoughts and feelings.
Cognitive behavioural therapy is an effective treatment for depression and anxiety.
Medication can help correct chemical imbalances in the brain.
Take your mental health medication every day as prescribed.
Do not stop your mental health medication without consulting your doctor.
Recovery from mental illness is possible with the right treatment and support.
Support from family and friends is vital for mental health recovery.
Reduce stigma by treating people with mental illness with respect.
Do not use hurtful language when talking about mental health.
Educate yourself and others about mental health conditions.
Self-care is an important part of maintaining good mental health.
Practice relaxation techniques such as deep breathing and meditation.
Spend time in nature to improve your mood and reduce stress.
Physical activity is one of the most effective ways to improve mental health.
Maintain social connections to protect your mental health.
Limit alcohol and drug use to protect your mental health.
Set realistic goals and celebrate small achievements.
Be kind to yourself and avoid negative self-talk.
Seek help if you are having thoughts of harming yourself.
Suicide is preventable with the right support and intervention.
Crisis support lines are available if you need immediate help.
You are not alone — help is available and recovery is possible.
Mental health awareness reduces stigma and encourages help-seeking.
Workplaces should support employees with mental health problems.
Schools should provide mental health support for learners.
Communities play an important role in supporting mental health.
Traditional healers and faith leaders can complement mental health care.
Integrate mental health care into your overall healthcare routine.
Mental health and physical health are closely connected.
Addressing mental health improves outcomes for all chronic conditions.
Invest in your mental health as you would invest in your physical health.
A mentally healthy community is a productive and thriving community.
Speak up about mental health and help break the silence.
Your mental health matters and you deserve support and care.
Reaching out for help is a sign of strength not weakness.
Every step towards better mental health is worth celebrating.
You have the power to improve your mental health one day at a time.
Mental health is a journey and every journey begins with a single step.
Together we can build a world where mental health is valued and protected.
Community health workers are trained to provide basic health services.
Community health workers can visit you at home for health support.
Ask your community health worker about health services in your area.
Community health campaigns provide free testing and treatment.
Attend community health days to access free health services.
Health promotion activities educate communities about disease prevention.
School health programmes provide health education and services to learners.
Workplace wellness programmes support the health of employees.
Faith communities play an important role in health promotion.
Traditional leaders can support health campaigns in their communities.
Community gardens improve food security and nutrition.
Clean water and sanitation are essential for community health.
Advocate for clean water and proper sanitation in your community.
Environmental health affects the health of the entire community.
Report environmental health hazards to the local authorities.
Air pollution increases the risk of respiratory diseases.
Reduce indoor air pollution by improving ventilation in your home.
Avoid burning waste near homes and communities.
Safe roads and public spaces reduce the risk of injuries.
Road traffic accidents are a major cause of death and disability.
Wear a seatbelt every time you travel in a vehicle.
Do not use your phone while driving.
Never drink and drive.
Pedestrians should use designated crossings and walkways.
Cyclists should wear helmets and use designated lanes.
Drowning prevention requires supervision near water at all times.
Teach children to swim to reduce the risk of drowning.
Fire safety education prevents burns and fire-related deaths.
Install smoke detectors in your home.
Keep a first aid kit at home and know how to use it.
Learn basic first aid skills to help in an emergency.
Know how to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
Call for emergency help immediately in a life-threatening situation.
Do not move an injured person unless they are in immediate danger.
Occupational health protects workers from work-related illnesses.
Wear personal protective equipment in hazardous work environments.
Report work-related injuries and illnesses to your employer.
Ergonomics reduces the risk of musculoskeletal injuries at work.
Take regular breaks to prevent fatigue and injury at work.
Ageing is a natural process that requires ongoing health management.
Older adults should have regular health check-ups.
Falls are a leading cause of injury in older adults.
Remove hazards in the home to prevent falls in older adults.
Social isolation increases the risk of depression in older adults.
Encourage older adults to stay socially active and engaged.
Dementia is a condition that affects memory and daily functioning.
Early diagnosis of dementia allows for better planning and support.
Caregivers of people with dementia also need support and rest.
Palliative care improves the quality of life for people with serious illness.
Hospice care provides comfort and dignity at the end of life.
Advance care planning allows you to express your wishes for end-of-life care.
Grief and bereavement support is available after the loss of a loved one.
Health literacy empowers communities to make informed health decisions.
Access to health information is a right for all community members.
Digital health tools can help you manage your health more effectively.
Use reliable sources of health information such as the clinic and health department.
Avoid spreading unverified health information on social media.
Verify health information with a qualified healthcare professional.
Together we can build healthier and stronger communities.
Health is wealth — invest in it every single day.
Understanding the difference between a virus and a bacteria helps you know why antibiotics are not always needed.
Antibiotics should only be taken when prescribed by a doctor.
Never demand antibiotics from your doctor if they are not necessary.
Overuse of antibiotics leads to antibiotic resistance.
Antibiotic resistance is a serious global health threat.
Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
Painkillers should be used with caution and only as directed.
Over-the-counter medications can have serious side effects if misused.
Always read the dosage instructions before taking any medication.
Do not give adult medications to children without medical advice.
Children require different medication doses based on their weight and age.
Herbal and traditional medicines can interact with prescription medications.
Always inform your doctor if you are using any complementary therapies.
Health screening is recommended even when you feel well.
Many serious diseases develop silently without obvious symptoms.
Blood tests can reveal health problems before symptoms appear.
A healthy gut microbiome supports your immune system and overall health.
Probiotics found in yoghurt and fermented foods support gut health.
Chronic inflammation is linked to many serious diseases including cancer.
Reducing sugar and processed food intake lowers inflammation in the body.
Your lifestyle choices today determine your health outcomes tomorrow.
Taking responsibility for your health leads to a longer and better quality of life.
